title: Harold Battiste, the AFO label and the changing bass sound
summary: An audience member asks about Battiste; King mentions AFO, Barbara George, Sonny and Cher and Mac Rebennack on sessions.

blocks.x: I wanted to know if Harold Baptiste was the brains behind, what you call him, the brains behind? The brains behind? Yes. Oh, anybody.
I mean, who he got started? Who he really produced and all that?

stuff Yeah, it wasn't from here. Joe Turner. Joe Turner. So everything that we put in the bread basket was for artists away from here. And when Dick mentioned how, how played an integral part in, with the AFO record label where they were instituting the evolvement of the 50s music is right in 60, with I know that Barbara George taking and all that stuff come out right in that era right there. Well, the transition was taking place then with the R&B sound, the bass become dominant then, you know, on the recordings you hear. And, uh, Sonny and Cher, I think Harold knew Sonny and Cher when, before he left here. Yeah. Yeah. Like, uh, a lot of people didn't know that Max Rabinak used to play on a lot of the sessions with Harold Batiste during that period. With, uh, uh, yeah, for executives. Yeah.
